Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM6031 : Anatomy and Physiology { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I. Introduction to Human Body: Orientation, levels of structural organization and body systems, basic life processes, homeostasis, basic anatomical terminology.[2hrs]
Module II. Cellular and Tissue level Organization : Biochemistry / Enzymes, Cell Transport, Cell Communication, Endocrine System, Cell Division, Cancer, Tissues. [2hrs]
Module III. Muscular system: Anatomy of the Muscular System, Nerve conduction velocity assessment, Osmolality and specific gravity measurements, Neuromuscular Physiology: Electromyography for muscle strength and fatigue. [6 hrs]
Module IV. The Cardiovascular System: Anatomy of the Cardiovascular System, Cardiovascular Physiology: ECG interpretation, Heart auscultation, Pulse and blood pressure determination, Regulation of the cardiovascular system. [6hrs]
Module V. The Respiratory System: Anatomy of the respiratory System, Respiratory Physiology: Oxygen saturation, Blood gases assessment, Peak flow assessment, Spirometry, Respiratory rate and lung sound assessment, Regulation of respiratory system. [5hrs]
Module VI. The Digestive system: Anatomy of the Digestive System, Digestion process, Role of different accessory and secondary organs in digestion, Gastrointestinal Physiology: Flexible sigmoidoscopy.[7 hrs]
Module VII. The integumentary system: Structure and functions of skin. [3 hrs]
Module VIII. Integrative Physiology: Dietary plans, Endocrinology: Blood glucose determination
First Aid: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (chest compression, external defibrillation), Rehydration choices, Endotracheal intubation. [8 hrs]

Course Objective

1 .

To learn the structural and functional components of human body
2 .

To correlate the structural and functions of the organs and organ systems with various diseases
3 .

To understand engineering principles involved in anatomy and physiology of human body.

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of the course the student will be able to
1. Explain the anatomy of the organ and organ systems of the human body.
2. Narrate the physiology of each organ to the maintenance of homeostasis.
3. Elucidate the physiological and pathological aspects of growth and development.
4. Explain the engineering principles involved in the anatomy and physiology of human body.
5. Understand the coordination between different organs and organ systems.

Essential Reading

1 .

Martini and Nath, Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology, Pearson , 11th ed,2018

2 .

Wood, Laboratory Manual for Anatomy and Physiology, Pearson , 6th ed,2017

Supplementary Reading

1 .

K. Saladin, Anatomy and Physiology, McGraw-Hill , 5th ed,2016

2 .

Richard S Snell, Clinical Anatomy by Regions, Lippincott Williams & Wilkins , 8th edition, 2007

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CH2211 : Chemical Process Calculations { 2-1-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Engineering Calculations: Units and dimensions Conversion of units. Chemical reactions: excess reactant, limiting reactant, conversion, extent of reaction yield and selectivity in multiple reactions Composition of mixtures and solutions. Flow-sheeting: degrees of freedom and its importance in flow-sheeting. Material balance with and without chemical reactions: Recycle, bypass, and purge calculations calculations for unit operations like mixing, evaporation, crystallization and distillation Combustion reactions. Behavior of ideal gases: Various equations of state, Law of Dalton and Amagat, Densities of gaseous mixture. Real gases: Critical properties, various equation of state, Law of corresponding states. Vapour pressures: Liquefaction, Vaporization, Cox Chart, Duhring Plot.Psychometric calculations. Energy balance: Heat capacity of gases, liquids, solids and solutions, Heats of fusion and vaporization, heat of reaction, heat of combustion, heat of formation enthalpy change. Fuel calculations adiabatic flame temperature. Numerical techniques for solving material and energy balance equations Vapour–liquid equilibrium calculations. Use of spreadsheet software (Excel/Origin).

Course Objective

1 .

It aims at providing fundamental knowledge of chemical engineering and application of this knowledge in the solving of material and energy balances of chemical processes.
2 .

Material Balance Calculations: Fundamentals, Calculations for Single and Multiple Units Reaction Stoichiometry & Reactive Processes Combustion reactions, Introduction to Single- & Multi-phase SystemsRecycle & Bypass, Introduction to Chemical Reaction Stoichiometry
3 .

Introduction to Energy Balance & Basic Concepts Energy Balance with & without Chemical Reaction
4 .

Humidity and Psychrometric Chart Computing and Simulation for solving multi-equation balance problems

Course Outcome

1 .

Help the students to understand basic chemical engineering concepts and methods of analysis. ToEnrich the knowledge of students to systems of units and measurement scales, chemical process types, process flow diagrams, steady-state mass balance calculations for batch and continuous processes applied to solution of problems in systems of interest to chemical process industries

Course Details

Subject Nature : Practical

Module 1 :

• Estimation of carbonyl group in organic compounds
• Estimation of hydroxyl group in organic compounds
• Estimation of amine group in organic compounds
• Estimation of sugars using quantitative methods

7557.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EE6241 : Electrical Insulation in Power Systems { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module-I: Introduction to Electrical Insulation In Power Systems: Properties of dielectrics, Classification and applications, Design parameters. (2 Hrs)
Module-II: Gas Dielectrics: Gas behaviour under Zero electric field, Generation of charged particle, Deionization processes, Uniform & Non-uniform field gas breakdown, Choice of dielectric Gases. (4 Hrs)
Module-III: Air Insulation: Air insulation application, voltage stresses, Impulse breakdown probability, BDV Characteristics, V-T curve and Insulation coordination, Phase to Phase BDV characteristics, Arc discharge, Undesirable effect of corona, Television interference. (5 Hrs)
Module-IV: SF6 Insulation: Basic properties, Uniform & Non-uniform field breakdown, Estimation of minimum discharge voltages, Factors affecting discharge voltages, Arc interruption, GIS, GI cables, SF6 gas handling & application. (4 Hrs)
Module-V: Liquid Dielectrics: Classification of Insulating Oils, Characteristics & Reconditioning of Insulating Oils, Electric conduction & Breakdown of Liquids. (2 Hrs)
Module-VI: Solid Dielectrics: Solid Insulating Materials, Dielectric Loss, Breakdown, Vacuum Dielectrics: Pre-breakdown in vacuum, Factors affecting BDV in vacuum, BD mechanisms, VCB. (3 Hrs)
Module-VII: Composite Dielectrics: Dielectric properties, edge breakdown, Cavity breakdown, Breakdown due to surface Erosion and tracking, Chemical and Electromechanical deterioration, Materials of outdoor Insulators, Oil-Impressed Insulation. (7 Hrs)
Module-VIII: High-Voltage Cables: Cable Materials, Type of Cables, Electric stress in cables, Cable losses, Partial discharge in Cables, Treeing in Cables, Cable aging and life estimation, Cable fault Location, Recent advances in Cable Technology. (4 Hrs)
Module-IX: New Measurement and Diagnostic Technologies: Digital Impulse recorder, Digital Technique in HV Test, Testing automation, Electric field measurements, Electro-optic Sensor, Magneto-optic sensor, Measurement of very fast transient in GIS, Space charge measurement, Electro optical imaging Technique. (5 Hrs)

Course Objective

1 .

To learn about material composition, properties, breakdown characteristic of different type of Solid, Liquid, gas and composite insulation and its application.
2 .

To learn about the materials of outdoor Insulators, Oil-Impressed Insulation.
3 .

To learn about the different types of High-Voltage Cables and its diagnosis method.
4 .

To learn about the New Measurement and Diagnostic Technologies for condition monitoring of HV insulation.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Students learn about the recent trends in insulation used in power system.
2. Students learn about breakdown characteristic of different type Solid, Liquid and Gas insulation.
3. Students will learn about the composite insulation used in the power system.
4. Students can calculate electromagnetic field distribution of HV Insulation used.
5. To understand the use of HV cable in different applied voltage.
6. Students will get exposure to new measurement and diagnostic technologies.

Essential Reading

1 .

Nazar Hussain Malik, A. A. Al-Arainy, and Mohammad Iqbal Qureshi, Electrical Insulation in Power System, CRC Press , New York, 1971

2 .

Andrew R. Hilema, Insulation Coordination for Power Systems, CRC Press , 1991

Supplementary Reading

1 .

J. P. Holtzhausen, W L Vosloo, High Voltage Engineering Practice and Theory, CRC Press, 2 edition , 2000

2 .

R. Arora and W. Mosch, High Voltage and Electrical Insulation Engineering, IEEE Press, John Willy & Sons publication,New Jersey , 2010

8069.t: MN5244: Coal Bed Methane and CO2 Sequestration
8069.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : MN5244 : Coal Bed Methane and CO2 Sequestration { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: 4 classes
Introduction to various reservoirs, conventional and unconventional reservoirs, inherent properties, production and gas recovery, Coalbed methane (CBM) introduction, worldwide distribution,
Module 2: 8 classes
Coal structure and properties, Classifications of coal with rank, grade, composition and their importance, organic structures, maturity, pore distributions, adsorption, diffusion and fluid flow fundamentals, production and recovery, field patterns and results.
Module 3: 9 classes
Gas storage capacity and Fluid flow: Key factors, detailed discussions, associated tests, gas-in-place and gas content analysis, sorption time, permeability effects, shrinkage and swelling effects. Uncertainty analysis. Examples from various case studies.
Module 4: 9 classes
Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS): Fundamentals, CCS options, geological sequestration technologies, ECBM and CO2 Sequestration: Importance, associated problems. Field drillhole pattern/design, cyclic, non-cyclic and/or continuous injections and their results. Reservoir Simulation.
Module 5: 4 classes
Different test procedures in CBM: Proximate and Petrographic analysis, Isotherm test, Desorption canister test. Gas Injection and Displacement.
Class tests: 2
Total Classes: 36

Course Objective

1 .

To understand the structures of unconventional reservoir like CBM, storage and transport properties, production cycles.
2 .

To know the planning and design aspects for the smooth production from the CBM reservoirs.
3 .

To learn the experimental methods for gas recovery in laboratory and design and simulation techniques for field studies.

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: To identify various unconventional reservoirs and their importance for sustainable gas exploration.
CO2: To understand the factors influencing the production performance of CBM reservoirs.
CO3: To learn about the various gas characterization and gas sorption properties for laboratory and field experiments.
CO4: To analyze planning and design requirements for fluid flow and gas transport.
CO5: To know about the current and possible future challenges for the environment and mitigate them.

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EE2740 : Electronic Circuits Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Analog circuits 12 hr.
• Characterization of Simple and Cascade Current Mirror circuits (BJT and MOSFET)
• Design of differential amplifier with resistive load (BJT) and active load (MOSFET)
• Design of R-C and L-C oscillators (phase shift/Wein Bridge/Colpitt/Hartley)
• Design of a second order active filter (low pass/high pass)
• Study and Design of Power Amplifiers (Push Pull/Class A).
Module 2: Digital Circuits 6hr.
• Study of basic logic gates and universal logic gates Realization of logic circuits using universal logic gates. To construct and verify the operation of single digit and multi digit half adder, Full adder / subtractor using logic gates and IC 7483.
• Comparison of Sequential and Combinational Logic Circuits Study of Digital to Analog converter by weighted resistance method. Design and verification of A/D converter Study of Seven Segment Display Technique using IC 7447/ 7446.
• . To study the characteristics and operation of a programmable Shift Register using IC 7495 Verification of UP/ DOWN count using IC 74193.
• Study of Ring and Decade Johnson Ring counters using ICs and Flip- Flops.
Module 3:Simulation Using HDL /Verilog 10 hr.
• (i) Static and Dynamic Characteristic of NAND and Schmitt-NAND gate(both TTL and MOS) Synthesis of a logic function by NAND gates only. (Minimized and two level).
• (ii) Measurement of delay of the logic sp synthesized Design a clock by using NAND gates and R-C network as well as crystal
• (iii) Study the functionality of Multiplexer and using it design and implement a logic circuit
• (iv) Study the principle of a Demultiplexer and implement multi-output logic circuit
• (v) Experiment on Serial-in, Parallel-in Serial-out right shift register with preset and clear.
• (vi) Generate maximally long linear sequence using this shift register and other necessary logic gates.
• (vii) Study the dynamic characteristic of a J-K flip-flop and hence find out maximum operational frequency
• (viii)Design a ripple modulo counter and set-rest feedback method. Verify the states of count.
• (ix) Determine each stage delay and total delay. Determine the maximum clock frequency that it is able to count
• (x) Design a sequential circuit and implement it by J-K flip-flops and other related logic gates.

Course Objective

1 .

To illustrate the students different electronic circuit and their application in practice.
2 .

To impart knowledge on assessing performance of electronic circuit through monitoring
3 .

To evaluate the use of computer-based analysis tools to review performance of semiconductor device circuit.
4 .

To know the concepts of Combinational circuits, flipflops, registers and counters. To evaluate the use of Verilog/HDL tool for designing digital circuit.

Course Outcome

1 .

The students will be able to :
CO 1: Set up testing strategies and select proper instruments to evaluate performance
characteristics of electronic circuit.
CO2: Choose testing and experimental procedures on different types of electronic circuit and
analyze their operation different operating conditions.
CO3: Evaluate possible causes of discrepancy in practical experimental observations in
comparison to theory.
CO4: Practice different types of wiring and instruments connections keeping in mind
technical, Economical, safety issues.
CO5: Prepare professional quality textual and graphical presentations of laboratory data and
Computational results, incorporating accepted data analysis and synthesis methods,
Mathematical software and word-processing tools.
